dexie_schema.name: health

stores.cache: key, fetched_at — {key: path|day, path, day, body, fetched_at}: the last answer of every GET
stores.outbox: ++seq, &id, state, next_at — {id (ULID), kind, method, path, body, day, created_at, attempts, next_at, state: waiting|failed, last_error}
stores.session: id — {id: 'current', started_at, data}: the training session in progress
stores.settings: key — {key, value}: access_key, theme, debug_engine_down, install_skipped

migration_plan: A new version only adds stores or indexes; the outbox and the session are never renamed or dropped while they can hold something the engine has not received.
The cache can be cleared in upgrade() whenever its shape changes: it is rebuilt from the engine.
On versionchange the connection closes (a newer tab or version opened).
Every new version gets a fake-indexeddb test that upgrades a v(n-1) database holding data.

cache_first_pattern: useCached(db, path, day, ctx) / cacheFirst(): show the saved answer for (path, day) at once with state 'loading', ask the engine, then show the new answer ('fresh') and keep it.
When the engine does not answer, the saved answer stays with the reason as its state: offline, engine_unavailable, unauthorized, rejected or server. It is never replaced by an error.
Under the data, <Freshness view> says 'Updated N min ago' quietly, or 'Showing saved data · Updated N min ago.' and the reason.
A screen with nothing saved and no answer says why instead of rendering blank; a screen that throws shows a message (ScreenBoundary) and the tab bar stays.
outbox_contract: Every write goes through enqueue(db, {kind, method, path, body, day}): the phone mints its ULID; the engine's saves are idempotent on the ids the body carries (rebuild rule 4).
Sent strictly in the order written (seq), each with its own X-Local-Date (the day it was written).
Offline, the engine starting or down, or a 5xx: the item waits 5 s, 15 s, 1 min, 5 min, then 15 min, and nothing after it overtakes it.
A refusal (4xx): the item is kept as 'failed' with the engine's code and the queue goes on; Settings sends it again on the owner's tap.
A wrong key (401): the queue stops until the key changes; every item stays.
An item leaves the outbox ONLY on a 2xx. Back online, every waiting item may go at once. The loop runs at the start, after each write, when the app comes to the front, and when the first wait ends.
With Supabase as the system of record a 2xx means the store has the row (the engine waits for Supabase before it answers), so there is no mirror_warning to keep.
service_worker_rules: Precache the shell only (index.html, the CSS, the JS, the manifest, the logo); Eruda and the splash screens stay out.
Every navigation is answered with the precached index.html, /api excluded; there is NO route for /api, so it always goes to the network and the phone's database owns the data.

clientsClaim on the first install; a new version WAITS and takes over (SKIP_WAITING) only when the app starts or comes to the front with no training session (lib/updates.ts mayTakeUpdate); a timer reloads too because iOS does not always fire controllerchange.
Registered with updateViaCache 'none' so a new sw.js is always fetched.
